Rashi on Pesachim 48a:10:1.hebrew: דלא חזיא לא לדידיה ולא לאורחים - והרי סופו ליטול אחת לחלה, שאין דרך לבצוע מכל אחת:
Rashi on Pesachim 48a:10:1.english: That is not fit neither for him nor for guests - For indeed, in the end he will take one [loaf] for challah, since it is not the practice to break off [a piece] from each one.

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:10:2.hebrew: אבל הכא - דכולהו חזו לאורחין ואורחין שכיחי, אמרינן "הואיל" למישרייה. ואי קשיא: הא דאמר ר' יהושע "לא זהו חמץ שמוזהרין כו'", אלמא לית ליה "הואיל ואי בעי מיתשל עלה" אפילו לחומרא, וכל שכן "הואיל" דהכא לקולא — לא דמי, דהשתא מיהא לאו דידיה הוא; וכך שמעתי. ומגמגם לבי עלה. ונראה בעיני, דאין "הואיל" בזה, בדבר שאינו שלו, דנימא "הואיל ואי בעי מייתי ליה ברשותיה". דאם כן, הקדש דקיימא לן "אבל אתה רואה של גבוה" ולא פליג ר"א — הא אי בעי פריק ליה והוי דידיה! ואף סוגיא דשמעתא לא מייתבא שפיר. וכמדומה דפירוש הכתוב ברישא דשמעתא — "הואיל ואי בעי מיתשיל עליה" — לא גר', אלא הכי גר': "ר' אליעזר סבר אמרינן 'הואיל', ור' יהושע סבר לא אמרינן 'הואיל'". והכי פירושא: ר' אליעזר סבר שרי לאפותה, ואע"ג דסוף סוף איכא חדא דלא חזיא ליה, אין כאן איסור מלאכה, הואיל וכל חדא וחדא חזיא ליה, דמצי למשקל מכל חדא פורתא. ור' יהושע סבר לא אמרינן "הואיל", דהא סופו ליטול אחת מהן לחלה; הלכך, כיון דטובת הנאה אינה ממון ולא עבר עלה, מנחתה עד הערב וישרפנה:
Rashi on Pesachim 48a:10:2.english: But here - Since all of them are fit for guests and guests are common, we say "since" (ho'il) to permit it. And if you ask: [What about] that which Rabbi Yehoshua said, "This is not the chametz concerning which we are warned [not to see or possess] etc." — thus [it appears] he does not hold of "since if he wants he can ask [a sage to annul his designation] on it" even to be stringent, and all the more so [he would not hold of] "since" here to be lenient! — [the answer is that] it is not comparable, because now at least it is not his; and so I have heard. However, my heart wavers about this [explanation]. And it seems to me that "since" does not apply in this case — in a matter that is not his, such that we would say "since if he wants he could bring it into his possession" — for if so, [regarding] consecrated property (hekdesh), where we hold as an established rule, "but you may see [the chametz] of the Most High," and Rabbi Eliezer does not disagree [there], behold if he wants he could redeem it and it would become his! And furthermore, the flow of the sugya does not settle well [with that text]. And it seems to me that the explanation written at the beginning of the sugya — "since if he wants he can ask [to annul] it" — is not part of the Gemara text, rather this is the text: "Rabbi Eliezer holds we say 'since,' and Rabbi Yehoshua holds we do not say 'since.'" And this is its explanation: Rabbi Eliezer holds it is permitted to bake it, and even though ultimately there is one [loaf] that is not fit for him, there is no prohibition of labor here, since each and every one is fit for him, for he can take a small piece from each one. And Rabbi Yehoshua holds we do not say "since," for in the end he will take one of them for challah; therefore, since the benefit of discretion (tovat hana'ah) is not [considered] monetary value and he does not transgress on it, she leaves it until evening and burns it.

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:11:1.english: They said it - This [statement] of Rami bar Chama.

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:11:2.hebrew: מילתא דקשיא לן כו' - דבטובת הנאה ממון ליכא לאוקמי פלוגתייהו לחוד, דנהי נמי דטובת הנאה ממון לר' אליעזר, אפילו הכי השתא נמי עובר משום "לא תעשה כל מלאכה", ומוטב לעבור על "בל יראה" מאליו ואינו עושה מעשה בידים, מלעבור על "לא תעשה כל מלאכה" ועושה מעשה בידים:
Rashi on Pesachim 48a:11:2.english: A matter that has been difficult for us, etc. - For [with the principle that] the benefit of discretion is [considered] money, one cannot establish their dispute [on that] alone. For even though the benefit of discretion is [considered] money according to Rabbi Eliezer, even so, now too he transgresses on account of "You shall not do any work," and it is better to transgress "it shall not be seen" [which occurs] on its own while he does not perform an act with his hands, than to transgress "You shall not do any work" while performing an act with his hands.

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:12:1.english: My reason is because of “since” - And there is no desecration here.

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:13:1.hebrew: אהדר ליה במכילתא אחריתא - ואיכא למימר דבתרוייהו פליגי: ר' אליעזר סבר טובת הנאה ממון, הלכך אי מחמצה גביה עבר עלה, ולאפותה קודם לכן אין כאן איסור, דאמרי' הואיל, ואיכא למימר בכל חדא חזיא ליה. ור' יהושע סבר אינה ממון, הלכך לא זהו חמץ שמוזהרין עליו, וכי אפי לה עבר עלה, דלא אמרינן הואיל. והא דתריצנא לעיל דכולי עלמא טובת הנאה אינה ממון, אכתי לא שמיע לן הא דאהדר ליה ר' אליעזר לר' יהושע הרי הוא עובר בבל יראה:
Rashi on Pesachim 48a:13:1.english: He responded to him in a different tractate - And it is possible to say that they disagree regarding both [issues]: Rabbi Eliezer holds [that] the benefit of discretion [tovat hana'ah] is [considered] money; therefore, if it becomes leavened in his possession, he transgresses on account of it, and [as for] baking it beforehand, there is no prohibition here, for we say "since" [ho'il], as one can say regarding each [loaf] that it is fit for him. And Rabbi Yehoshua holds [that] it is not [considered] money; therefore, "this is not the leavened bread about which we are warned," and when he bakes it, he transgresses on account of it, because we do not say "since" [ho'il]. And [as for] that which we resolved earlier, that according to everyone the benefit of discretion is not [considered] money, we had not yet heard this [statement] where Rabbi Eliezer responded to Rabbi Yehoshua, "He transgresses [the prohibition of] 'it shall not be seen.'"

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:14:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with ben Beteira - She should place [it] into cold [water].

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:15:1.hebrew: שיעור עיסה - ללוש בפסח ולא יותר, שיכול לשומרה מידי חימוץ:
Rashi on Pesachim 48a:15:1.english: The measure of a dough - To knead on Passover, and no more, so that one can guard it from leavening.

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:15:2.english: The matters are reversed - For barley is closer to becoming leavened than wheat.

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:16:1.hebrew: הא בחסיכתא הא במעלייתא - קמייתא במעלייתא, בתרייתא בחסיכתא, ששלש שלהן אינן אלא קביים טובות:
Rashi on Pesachim 48a:16:1.english: This [refers] to low-quality [grain], that [refers] to high-quality [grain] - The first [baraita refers] to high-quality [grain], [and] the latter [baraita refers] to low-quality [grain], for three [kav] of them are only [equivalent to] two good [kav].

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:17:1.english: Learn from this - With respect to buying and selling.

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:17:2.hebrew: גריען חיטי חסיכתא ממעלייתא טפי ממאי דגריען שערי חסיכתא ממעלייתא - דאילו בחיטי קתני בטובות קביים וברעות שלשת קבים, אלמא גרעי תילתא. ואילו בשעורין, הטובות שלשת קבין והרעות ארבעה, ליכא גריעותא אלא ריבעא:
Rashi on Pesachim 48a:17:2.english: Low-quality wheat is worse than high-quality [wheat] more than low-quality barley is worse than high-quality [barley] - For whereas regarding wheat it teaches: for good [wheat], two kavim, and for inferior [wheat], three kavim — thus they are diminished by a third — whereas regarding barley, good [barley is] three kavim and inferior [barley is] four [kavim], there is only a diminution of a fourth.

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:18:1.english: A Melognaean kav - A kav of that place.

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:18:2.english: For Passover - Not to knead more [than this], so that one can guard it from leavening.

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:18:3.english: And similarly, for challah - With this measure of dough as well, all the days of the year, [it suffices] to become obligated in challah.

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:1:1.hebrew: מן המאתים - על כרחיך אנסכים קאי, וקאמר: הביאו הנסכים עליו מן המאתים, שישתיירו מאתים בבור היין:
Rashi on Pesachim 48a:1:1.english: Out of two hundred - Perforce [the verse] refers to libations, and says: Bring the libations with it [the offering] from the two hundred, [meaning] that two hundred [portions] remain in the wine vat.

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:1:2.hebrew: מכאן לערלה שבטלה במאתים - דאי לאו בשאיסור מעורב בו קאי, אמאי מצריך מאתים? ובעלמא בסיפרי נפקא לן שפיר דערלה וכלאי הכרם בטילין במאתים, והאי מכאן לאו דוקא, אלא אף כאן אתה יכול לסמוך קצת:
Rashi on Pesachim 48a:1:2.english: From here [it is derived] that orla is nullified in two hundred - For if [the verse] were not referring to [a case] where a forbidden [substance] is mixed into it, why would it require two hundred? Elsewhere, in the Sifrei, we properly derive that orla and kil'ei hakerem [diverse kinds of the vineyard] are nullified in two hundred; and this [expression], "from here," is not [meant] literally, rather even here you can rely [on it] slightly.

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:3:1.english: A prohibition of a different thing - [The prohibition of] Shabbat.

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:4:1.english: Wasn't it you who said - In [the chapter] Eilu Hen HaLokin (Makkot 21b).

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:4:2.hebrew: חילוק מלאכות לשבת - שאם עשה שתים בהעלם אחד או [אחת] בשתי העלמות, חייב שתים:
Rashi on Pesachim 48a:4:2.english: Division of labors for Shabbat - That if he performed two [labors] in one lapse of awareness, or one [labor] in two lapses of awareness, he is liable for two [sin-offerings].

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:4:3.hebrew: ואין חילוק מלאכות ליום טוב - שאם עשה שתי מלאכות במזיד, אינו לוקה שתים. והכא ביום טוב קיימינן, ומחייבת ליה משום י"ט תרתי, משום מוקצה ומשום מבשל גיד ביום טוב:
Rashi on Pesachim 48a:4:3.english: And there is no division of labors for a Festival - For if one performed two [prohibited] labors intentionally, he does not receive two [sets of] lashes. Yet here we are dealing with a Festival, and you hold him liable for two [sets of lashes] on account of the Festival — on account of muktzeh and on account of cooking the [sciatic] nerve on a Festival.

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:8:1.english: Rami bar Ḥama said: This [dispute] of Rabba and Rav Ḥisda - Where they disagreed regarding Yom Tov, whether we permit it because of [the principle of] "since" or not.

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:8:2.hebrew: מחלוקת רבי אליעזר ור' יהושע היא דרבי אליעזר סבר אמרינן הואיל - אע"ג דסופו להפריש אחת מהן לחלה, ונמצא שטרח בדבר שאינו ראוי לאכילה, אפי' הכי אמרינן הואיל ואי בעי לא מפריש חדא לחלה, אלא בצע מכל חדא וחדא, ואיכא למימר בכל חדא חזיא ליה, ומותר לאפותה:
Rashi on Pesachim 48a:8:2.english: [It] is a dispute between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua, as Rabbi Eliezer holds [that] we say "since" - Even though in the end he will separate one of them for challah, and it turns out that he exerted himself [over] something that is not fit for eating, even so we say "since" — [for] if he wishes, he does not separate one [whole loaf] for challah, rather he breaks off [a piece] from each and every one, and it can be said regarding each one [that] it is fit for him, and it is permitted to bake it.

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:8:3.hebrew: ור' יהושע סבר לא אמרינן הואיל - כדי להתיר מלאכות יום טוב. ואהואיל ואי בעי מיתשיל עלה דלעיל לא קאי רמי בר חמא, אלא אהואיל דאיסור מלאכת יום טוב:
Rashi on Pesachim 48a:8:3.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua holds: We do not say "since" - [i.e.,] in order to permit the labors of Yom Tov. And Rami bar Chama is not referring to the "since, if he wishes, he can request [annulment] of it" [mentioned] above; rather, [he is referring] to the "since" regarding the prohibition of Yom Tov labor.

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:9:1.hebrew: אלא דבעידנא דעיילי לה - איכא למימר בכל חדא וחדא חזיא ליה בלאו הואיל, דבכל חדא איכא למימר זו לא תהא לחלה:
Rashi on Pesachim 48a:9:1.english: Rather, because at the time that they place it [into the oven] - one can say regarding each and every [loaf] [that] it is fit for him [even] without [the principle of] ho'il ("since"), because regarding each one, one can say: "This one will not be for challah."

Rashi on Pesachim 48a:9:2.hebrew: אבל הכא דלאורחין הוא דחזיא - והרי עדיין לא זימן, לית ליה הואיל למישרייה לר' אליעזר:
Rashi on Pesachim 48a:9:2.english: However, here, where it is fit for guests - And behold, he has not yet invited [them], [so] Rabbi Eliezer does not hold [the principle of] "since" to permit it.

Tosafot on Pesachim 48a:14:1.hebrew: רבי אומר הלכה כר' אליעזר - ה"ר יוסף פסק כרבי משום דקיימא לן כוותיה מחבירו, וכן מנהג. ור"י דוחה, דשמא לא קאמר הכא כרבי מחבירו, דהא איפליגו רבה ורב חסדא בהכי; והא דהלכה כרבי מחבירו, היינו היכא דליכא פלוגתא דאמוראי:
Tosafot on Pesachim 48a:14:1.english: Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] says: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer - HaRav Rabbi Yosef ruled in accordance with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], because we hold [that the halakha is] in accordance with him over his colleague, and such is the custom. And Ri rejects [this], for perhaps [this rule] does not apply here [that the halakha is] in accordance with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] over his colleague, since Rabbah and Rav Chisda indeed disagreed about this; and that [rule] that the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] over his colleague applies where there is no dispute among Amoraim.
